analysis.title: Global Equity Market Arithmetic: Quantifying the speculative factor driving equity markets
key_insights: SG finds equity markets highly polarised, with many negative pairwise stock correlations driven by divergent AI and energy narratives. The correlation between long and short legs of momentum portfolios has collapsed and turned negative in the US.
PCA of excess stock returns: PC1 explains 27% of the variance in Japanese stock returns and 17% in the US, and has been relatively subdued in Europe. SG reads PC1 as speculative stock momentum.

A portfolio of the top 5% of MSCI ACWI stocks by prior 12-month price performance (120 of 2,400 global stocks) tracks PC1 closely. Its composition is 24% US, 21% China, 23% Taiwan, 9% Korea, 6% Japan and 10% other.
These high-momentum stocks are about 7% of total market cap but recently accounted for more than 25% of trading volume. SG calls this a different kind of concentration risk.

Sector correlations with PC1 match the AI theme: Capital Goods, Materials, Semiconductors and Tech Hardware are all positively correlated. SG concludes AI speculation has driven cross-sectional returns and that this speculative momentum now appears to be unwinding.
SG distinguishes the AI theme itself, which is struggling, from the speculation around it, which is under the most pressure because that is where the excess was greatest.

PC2 explains 7% of European stock return variance, 8% in the US and 4% in Japan. It appears to capture an energy/inflation dynamic that emerged with the rise in oil prices in Q1 2026. It correlates with Energy, Materials and Utilities, the last reflecting AI power demand.

Factor correlations: PC1 is high-volatility momentum with an anti-value bias. PC2 is momentum alongside lower risk, lower volatility and quality income. SG sees two versions of momentum coexisting, illustrated by the Nasdaq 100 vs the SG Quality Income index (SGQINTRD).
Week to 9 Nov 2026: S&P 500 closed at 7376.9 (-2.7% 1W, -5.7% 1M, +7.8% YTD). Nasdaq 100 closed at 26990.0 (-4.9% 1W, -13.6% 1M). The S&P 500 equal weighted index was -1.1% 1W and +1.7% 1M.

Japan was the weakest developed market: Nikkei 225 -9.3% 1W and -18.7% 1M, MSCI Japan -7.0% 1W in USD. KOSPI fell 11.7% in the week and 27.1% in the month. EM was -4.1% 1W and -13.8% 1M. India (BSE 100) rose 8.0% in the week.

Sector moves in the week, USD, World: Energy -9.7%, Technology -6.5%, Telecommunications -6.5%. Retail +5.1%, Travel and Leisure +4.8%. Over one month, World Technology was -17.4% and US Technology -16.1%, while Health Care was +9.4% and Consumer Staples +8.7%.
US SG momentum factor index fell 4.3% in the week and 5.7% in the month but is +23.9% YTD. Japan momentum fell 7.6% in the week and 13.9% in the month. US Value rose 8.1% in the month.

Monthly factor returns (long vs short): in the US, 12m1m price momentum was -21.4%, low vol +31.7%, low beta +33.1%, shareholder yield +24.3%, EV/EBITDA +19.0%, price/FCF +20.2%, FY1 EPS growth -20.4%, long-term growth -22.6%. Growth and momentum are being sold in favour of low risk and value.

Valuations: US 2026e P/E 20.5x and 2027e 17.5x, against World ex-US 13.5x and 12.2x for 2026e and 2027e. Consensus 2026e EPS growth is 32.7% for the US and 33.6% for the World, and 2027e growth is 17.2% for the US and 14.9% for the World.

Technology has the highest 2026e EPS growth among sectors in the US at 58.5% and 66.2% in the World, with Energy at 103.0% in the US (95.1% World) on oil. 2027e Energy EPS growth is -5.0% in the US and -6.4% in the World.
Regional 2026e EPS growth: Pacific ex Japan 124.1% (Korea 270.5%), World ex-US 37.7%, Europe 19.8%, UK 27.3%, Japan 24.8%, Emerging 26.5%. Taiwan growth is 73.1% for 2026e.

sector_views.rationale: These sectors correlate most with PC1, the speculative momentum factor SG says is unwinding. World Technology fell 17.4% in the month.
These sectors load on PC2, the energy/inflation factor tied to the Q1 2026 oil rise. World Energy fell 9.7% in the week but is +31.1% YTD.
Utilities correlate with PC2 as investors weigh AI power demand, not as a classic defensive sector.

sector_views.sector: Quality Income / defensives (Health Care, Consumer Staples)
sector_views.rationale: Quality Income outperformed the Nasdaq 100 on return/risk (1.715 vs 0.433). World Health Care was +9.4% and Consumer Staples +8.7% in the month.

earnings_insights: SG consensus 2026e EPS growth: US +32.7%, World +33.6%, Europe +19.8%, Japan +24.8%, Emerging +26.5%. These are FactSet bottom-up consensus estimates, not reported results.
SG consensus 2027e EPS growth (estimates): US +17.2%, World +14.9%, Europe +9.1%, Japan +11.5%, UK +4.2%.
The factor table shows negative EPS revision and surprise-trend factors in the month: in the US, 3m EPS revisions -10.6% and 3m EPS change (SUE) -17.8% (long vs short returns, not earnings figures).
Page 12 charts 4-week rolling EPS upgrades vs total estimate changes by region for FY1 and FY2, as of 30 Oct. The text does not give numeric values.

macro_indicators.reading: Rise in Q1 2026, no level given
macro_indicators.interpretation: SG ties PC2, the energy/inflation factor, to this rise, and the factor remains active alongside the AI factor.

risk_factors: Unwind of speculative AI-driven momentum, concentrated in US, Chinese, Taiwanese and Korean high-momentum stocks, and the high share of volume they account for.
Polarisation between the AI and energy/inflation narratives, with SG asking whether the two forms of momentum can coexist.
Japan and Korea are under heavy selling (Nikkei -9.3% and KOSPI -11.7% in the week).
Growth and earnings-revision factors are deeply negative across regions, so estimates may be under pressure.
charts_described: Chart on p.1: top 5% of MSCI ACWI momentum stocks vs S&P 500 PC1, which SG says tracks it closely.
Chart on p.1: top 5% momentum stocks are over 20% of market volume despite under 10% of market cap.
Chart on p.3: SG Quality Income vs Nasdaq 100 indexed, with return/risk of 1.715 for Quality Income, 0.433 for Nasdaq 100 and 1.169 for a 50/50 blend.
vol_and_positioning: High-momentum stocks (top 5% by 12-month performance) are about 7% of market cap but above 25% of recent trading volume, which SG calls a new kind of concentration risk.
US long-short momentum correlation has turned negative, and SG says the speculative AI-driven momentum appears to be unwinding.
Low vol, low beta and low risk factors strongly outperformed in the month: US low vol long-short +31.7%, low beta +33.1%, Merton distance to default +14.2%. US 4-week low vol was +29.5%.
US 12m1m price momentum long-short was -21.4% in the month and -19.9% over 4 weeks. Japan was -27.2% in the month.
US 1m reversal factors were positive in the month (+8.0% price reversals) and +14.9% over 26 weeks.

tension_points.bull_case: The AI theme itself is struggling but not broken. Consensus 2026e Technology EPS growth is 58.5% in the US and 66.2% in the World, and SG's Nasdaq 100 YTD is +6.9%.
tension_points.bear_case: SG says speculative momentum tied to AI appears to be unwinding, with the top-5% momentum names at 7% of market cap but over 25% of volume. World Technology fell 17.4% in one month and momentum factors turned sharply negative.

tension_points.bull_case: SG Quality Income and the Nasdaq 100 have both held up over the period, suggesting PC1 (high-vol momentum) and PC2 (lower-risk momentum) can coexist.
tension_points.bear_case: The factor correlations show PC1 has an anti-value, high-volatility bias and PC2 a low-volatility bias, so SG questions whether the two can coexist. PC1 is now unwinding.
